nodes.name: Co-MoS2-xCO hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co-MoS2-xCO composites (x = 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 1.4 MPa, representing CO pressure) were synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal method under CO atmosphere. Briefly, 0.5 mmol of (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O, 15 mmol of thiourea (CS(NH2)2), and 0.39 mmol of Co(NO3)2·6H2O were dissolved in 40 mL deionized water with magnetic stirring at 600 rpm for 30 min to form a homogeneous solution. The solution was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, where air was purged by 10 cycles of CO flushing. The autoclave was then pressurized with CO to 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, or 1.4 MPa (x = 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 1.4 corresponding to these CO pressures, respectively), sealed, and maintained at 175°C with continuous stirring at 600 rpm for 20 h. The product was collected by centrifugation, washed with deionized water and ethanol for 3 cycles (each solvent used once per cycle), and dried at 60°C for 6 h. All samples were further annealed in a tube furnace under an argon flow (50 mL/min): the temperature was raised to 350°C at a heating rate of 5°C/min and held at 350°C for 2 h, yielding the final Co-MoS2-xCO.

nodes.name: Ru impregnation and annealing
nodes.procedure: 0.3 g of Co-MoS2-CO (0.3 MPa CO) was dispersed in 30 mL deionized water by ultrasonication for 20 min. A stoichiometric RuCl3 aqueous solution (to reach 8 wt% nominal Ru loading) was added dropwise under magnetic stirring (600 rpm). The mixture was heated to 80°C in an oil bath for 3 h for complete Ru adsorption. After cooling to room temperature, the solid was collected by centrifugation (9000 rpm, 5 min), washed with deionized water and ethanol, then vacuum-dried at 60°C for 6 h. To enhance metal-support interaction, the precursor was annealed in 99.999% Ar (50 mL/min) at 5°C/min to 300°C, held for 2 h.

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance of Ru8%@MoS2 in 1 M KOH

nodes.characterization_summary: Layered morphology with distinct structural defects and interlayer spacing of 6.3 Å. No distinct Ru species observed, indicating uniform dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a–d respectively presents the TEM, HRTEM, and EDX mapping results of Ru8%@Co-MoS2-CO. A layered morphology with distinct structural defects is clearly observed in Fig. 1a and b.

nodes.characterization_summary: Interlayer spacing measured as 6.3 Å, consistent with XRD results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured interlayer spacing of 6.3 Å (Fig. 1c) is consistent with the X-ray diffraction (XRD) results (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform dispersion of Ru, Mo, S, and Co elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This observation is further corroborated by the EDX mapping of Fig. 1d of element Ru displaying the uniform dispersion of Ru.

properties.description: Elemental distribution maps with scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: Actual Ru loading of 7.3 wt%, Co 2.7 wt%, Mo 51.8 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The actual Ru loading quantified via ICP analysis was determined to be 7.3 wt% (Table S8), which is in close agreement with the nominal value of 8 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic MoS2 peaks at 14.0°, 33.6°, 59.9° for (002), (100), (110) planes. Peak shift from 12.8° to 14.0° indicates NHx elimination. No Ru or Co oxide peaks, indicating high dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Characteristic diffraction peaks of MoS2 are observed at 14.0°, 33.6°, and 59.9°, which correspond to the (002), (100), and (110) crystal planes, respectively (JCPDS 37-1492).

nodes.characterization_summary: 2H-MoS2 peaks at 281, 373, 405 cm⁻¹ (E1g, E2g¹, A1g). 1T phase peaks at 145, 235, 335 cm⁻¹ observed, especially in Co-MoS2-CO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy was employed to characterize the phase structures (2H and 1T phase) of the synthesized samples. As shown in Figs. 2b and S2b, in addition to 2H-MoS2 (E1g, E2g¹, and A1g, with characteristic peaks of 281, 373, and 405 cm⁻¹, respectively).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-MoS2-CO shows highest Sv content (1.382×10¹²). Ru8%@Co-MoS2-CO shows reduced EPR signal after Ru loading, indicating anchoring at Sv sites. Pristine MoS2: 7.347×10¹¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co-MoS2-CO displays the strongest EPR signal and highest amounts of Sv (1.382×10¹²). This observation is attributed to the synergistic effect of Co doping and the strong structure-directing role of CO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3d5/2 peaks at 280.4 eV (Ru⁰), 281.0 eV (Ru²⁺ S-coordinated), 281.7 eV (Ru⁴⁺ RuOx), mainly Ru²⁺ state with positive binding energy shift indicating electron transfer from Ru. Mo 3d shows 2H (81.6%) and 1T (11.6%) phases. Co 2p3/2: Co³⁺-S at 781.3 eV, Co⁰ at 779.0 eV, Co²⁺ at 783.8 eV, Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio = 2.0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru species of Ru⁰, Ru²⁺ (S-coordinated) and Ru⁴⁺ (RuOx) can be clearly observed for Ru8%@Co-MoS2-CO with the binding energy being respectively located 280.4, 281.0, and 281.7 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 35.4 mF cm⁻², indicating largest active site exposure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru8%@Co-MoS2-CO exhibits the highest Cdl value (Fig. 3d) of 35.4 mF cm⁻², indicating exposure of largest amounts of active sites than other counterparts.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance Rct = 21.8 Ω, lowest among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS, Fig. 3e and Table S2) shows that Ru8%@Co-MoS2-CO has the lowest charge transfer resistance (Rct = 21.8 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Higher hydrogen oxidation current and tip current confirm enhanced HER activity and electrical conductivity compared to Ru8%@MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Fig. 5a, the hydrogen oxidation current of Ru8%@Co-MoS2-CO was higher than that of Ru8%@MoS2, which confirms the significant enhancement of HER activity.
